item.title: Mainland criticizes Taiwan's DPP and separatists for political smear tactics
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Mainland criticizes Taiwan's DPP and separatists for political smear tactics Source: chinadaily.com.cnUpdated: 2026-10-21
The Chinese mainland on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities and diehard "Taiwan independence" separatists for colluding to smear the mainland for their own political gain. In June 2025, the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office announced sanctions against a company headed by Shen Tu-cheng, the father of Shen Pao-yang, who was designated by the mainland as a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist in 2024. According to a recent media report, Shen Tu-cheng continued to purchase goods from the mainland and sell them overseas for a profit through another company under his name, VWAY. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the office, said at a press conference that the facts of the case are clear and the evidence is conclusive. Shen Pao-yang had resorted to various forms of sophistry in an attempt to mislead the public and divert attention, she said. "This fully exposes his guilty conscience, cowardice, and despicable character," Zhang added. On Oct 14, the mainland announced sanctions against VWAY, the new company owned by Shen Tu-cheng, including a ban on the company conducting transactions or cooperation with mainland organizations, enterprises, and individuals. Taiwan's "mainland affairs council" claimed that the mainland's sanctions and related measures were intended to "interfere in Taiwan's elections". Zhang stressed that the mainland protects the legitimate rights and interests of Taiwan compatriots in accordance with the law but will never tolerate diehard "Taiwan independence" separatists and their affiliated enterprises that undermine the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and obstruct cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation. "The DPP authorities and diehard 'Taiwan independence' separatists are colluding with each other and taking the opportunity to attack and smear the mainland for their own political gain," Zhang said, describing their actions as "despicable". item.title: Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities for hindering cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Mainland denounces Taiwan authorities for hindering cross-Strait exchanges Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-21
BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized the Taiwan authorities for barring relevant people on the island from attending the commemorative event held on the mainland marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen. Sun, a founding figure of the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) and a revered revolutionary leader who played a pivotal role in overthrowing imperial rule in China, died in 1925 in Beijing. His remains rest at the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum in Nanjing, east China's Jiangsu Province. Zhang Han, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, noted that the grand commemoration of Sun's legacy is intended to inherit and carry forward his noble spirit of upholding national unity and striving for national rejuvenation. She stressed that the move by Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities to obstruct cross-Strait exchanges and suppress Taiwan compatriots fully exposes their vicious intentions of betraying the nation and history, seeking to split the country, and stoking confrontation across the Taiwan Strait. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the KMT about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Recently, Taiwan authorities also rejected an application by mainland actor Zhang Linghe to visit the island for cultural exchanges. Zhang Han criticized this decision as politically motivated, saying it undermined cross-Strait cultural exchanges and ran counter to the desire of people on both sides for closer ties. She urged the DPP authorities to respect this shared desire, abandon political maneuvering, lift unreasonable restrictions and facilitate cultural exchanges across the Strait. The spokesperson also commented on a recent incident involving singer Jay Chou from Taiwan, who reposted and liked a video in which he was introduced as a "Chinese singer." The move drew praise from some internet users on both sides of the Strait, while pro-DPP figures criticized it. Zhang stressed that people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait are all Chinese. She slammed "Taiwan independence" secessionists for opposing the close bonds between people across the Strait and seeking to use political means to restrict legitimate expression by Taiwan residents, saying such actions reflected malicious intent and lacked public support. item.title: Mainland slams Taiwan's LNG pipeline investment as political maneuvering
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
Mainland slams Taiwan's LNG pipeline investment as political maneuvering Source: chinadaily.com.cnUpdated: 2026-10-21
A Chinese mainland spokeswoman stated on Wednesday that Taiwan's proposed purchase of liquefied natural gas from a project in Alaska reflects the Democratic Progressive Party authorities' attempts to curry favor with the United States at Taiwan's expense. Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular news conference. According to media reports, the DPP authorities have agreed to purchase 30 percent of the natural gas from an LNG pipeline project in Alaska and invest an additional $4.4 billion to ensure the project's completion. Taiwan's economic affairs department confirmed on Oct 14 that the island will purchase 6 million metric tons of LNG from the project each year once production begins. In response, Zhang criticized the DPP authorities for seeking to curry favor with the US at Taiwan's expense and pursuing "Taiwan independence" by relying on US support. "Such attempts will not succeed," she said. Taiwan relies heavily on imported energy, with more than 95 percent of its energy needs met by overseas supplies. Crude oil, LNG, and coal account for the bulk of its energy mix. Related Stories

item.title: Taiwan residents' trips to mainland rise nearly 20% in first eight months
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Taiwan residents' trips to mainland rise nearly 20% in first eight months Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-10-19
TAIPEI -- Taiwan residents made more than 2.49 million trips to the Chinese mainland in the first eight months of 2026, up 19.63 percent year-on-year, according to the island's tourism department. The mainland remained Taiwan residents' second-most popular outbound travel destination in the eight months, according to the department's latest figures. Monthly trips to the mainland exceeded 300,000 from March through August, with double-digit year-on-year growth recorded in each month. Overall outbound trips by Taiwan residents grew 15.24 percent in the first eight months, indicating that travel to the mainland expanded faster than outbound travel overall. Travel preferences vary across generations, according to Sun, a student at Taiwan Normal University. Older travelers often join group tours to destinations such as Xinjiang and Yunnan known for picturesque landscapes, while younger people favor independent trips to cities such as Chongqing and Shanghai, sometimes inspired by posts on Xiaohongshu, a lifestyle-focused social media platform. "People around me are traveling to the mainland more often, and many are happy to post photos and share their experiences on social media," Sun said. A Taipei resident also surnamed Sun, who has visited the mainland several times, cited the shared language, convenient transportation, and cultural similarities as reasons for returning. Tsai Tsung-yu, chairman of Taiwan-based Yu Sheng International Travel Service Co Ltd, confirmed that his company's group tours to the mainland increased this year. He attributed the destination's appeal to its varied landscapes and diverse food culture, which offer Taiwan travelers a broad range of experiences. Related Stories

item.title: Xu Clan Members from Taiwan Return to Jiaoling to Trace Roots and Honor Ancestors
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Xu Clan Members from Taiwan Return to Jiaoling to Trace Roots and Honor Ancestors Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-16
Oct 16(Taiwan.cn)—From October 9 to 10, a 32-member delegation from the Xu Clan Association of New Taipei City, Taiwan, and the Guo Xinggong Xu Clan Association returned to their ancestral home in Jiaoling for root-tracing, ancestor worship, and exchange activities. Long-separated clan relatives from both sides of the Taiwan Strait reunited, sharing the profound bond of common ancestry. On October 10, a grand ancestor worship ceremony was held. Early that morning, the clan group from Taiwan traveled to Yanjishan for the memorial rite. At the roadside, a stone carving bears the three powerful characters “Yan Gui Lai,” meaning “Swallows Return Home.” The imagery of “Beneath Yanjishan, swallows return to their nests; wanderers come back to their homeland” touched everyone present. Dressed in proper ceremonial attire, the group ascended the mountain path step by step to the ancestral tomb and completed the worship ritual following traditional etiquette. After the ceremony, the clansmen descended the mountain and visited the Xu Ancestral Hall and Dalu Bei Ancestral Shrine in succession. They paid homage to their forebears in accordance with rites, remembering the merits of their ancestors who pioneered and established their settlement. This homecoming ancestor worship event of the Xu clan constitutes a cross-Strait journey to trace ancestral roots, as well as an emotional gathering bound by shared blood. The Taiwan Strait cannot sever kinship ties, nor can time dilute this rooted affection. Taking clan kinship as the link and hometown sentiment as the bridge, the event further deepened and enhanced the fellowship between compatriots across the Strait. It once again bears witness to the shared cultural heritage and blood connection between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait.(Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Meizhou) Related Stories

item.title: Taiwan Compatriot Returns to Hometown to Seek Relatives and Honor Ancestors, Experiencing the Bond of Blood
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Taiwan Compatriot Returns to Hometown to Seek Relatives and Honor Ancestors, Experiencing the Bond of Blood Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-10-16
Oct 16(Taiwan.cn)—From September 24 to 29, Ms. Zhang Huilan, a compatriot from Taiwan, led a six-person group back to Xiangcheng County, Xuchang City, to seek relatives and pay homage to ancestors, fulfilling her long-cherished dream of a cross-Strait family reunion. Ms. Zhang Huilan is the daughter of Zhang Sheng'en, a veteran who moved to Taiwan. After her father passed away, she long harbored the wish to return to her hometown to look for her relatives. Through the joint efforts of all parties, Ms. Zhang's homecoming trip to trace her roots finally materialized. Welcomed by relatives and friends, Ms. Zhang and her entourage conducted root-tracing and ancestor worship activities at Sanligou Community, Cigou Subdistrict, Xiangcheng County, and at the ancestral tomb. They also visited scenic spots such as Ziyun Mountain and Shoushan Park. While enjoying the beautiful scenery, the closely related family members were immersed in the deep bonds of kinship. They talked about past stories and shared their visions for the future. Through this root-tracing trip, Ms. Zhang gained a deeper understanding of her family history, witnessed the new progress in her hometown's economic and social development, and felt a spiritual bond and sense of belonging to her ancestral home. An official from the Xuchang Taiwan Affairs Office stated that the office will use this root-seeking and ancestor worship activity as an opportunity to continue building bridges for exchanges between compatriots across the Taiwan Strait and serving as an emotional bond. It will help sustain the everlasting kinship between the two sides and contribute to the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland.(Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Xuchang) Related Stories

item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.

item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps
item.description:
Published: 2026-01-29
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-01-29
BEIJING, Jan. 28 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for hyping up the so-called information security risks of applications from the mainland. Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated at a press conference that the DPP moves have deprived people in Taiwan, especially the youth, of their right to know and the freedom to use social networking platforms. Noting that such moves reveal the fear and insecurity of the DPP authorities, Zhang said they will have to face the dire consequences of their wayward actions.
